hypotheses.justification: The statement mentions μH only through `HaarQuotient.density H μH`, a plain definition that needs no SFinite instance. In the proof, `SFinite μH` is used only by the helper `measurable_density` (for `lintegral_prod_right'`). `lintegral_density_mul_eq_one`, `lintegral_withDensity_eq_of_admissible` and `map_mk_withDensity_eq_smul_measure` do not take it. It is redundant given the other hypotheses. `hH : IsClosed (H : Set G)` gives `SigmaCompactSpace H` via `IsClosed.sigmaCompactSpace` (Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/SigmaCompact.lean:267), because G is locally compact and second countable and so σ-compact. Then `[μH.IsHaarMeasure]` gives `SigmaFinite μH` through the instance `MeasureTheory.Measure.IsHaarMeasure.sigmaFinite [SigmaCompactSpace G]` (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Group/Measure.lean:921), and `SFinite μH` follows from that. So the theorem stays true and provable after deleting it. The change to the proof is to add `haveI : SigmaCompactSpace H := hH.sigmaCompactSpace` before calling `measurable_density`. I did not check whether `[SFinite μ]` can also be dropped: the helper lemmas it feeds into depend on it, and I could not justify deleting it.
